description: Mirror the SONGS store into app.db via AppDatabase, following the Phase-5 ServiceOrderManager MIRROR pattern. Add a Songs table (DataJson + promoted columns), keyed by SongPathResolver.Normalize(Song.FolderPath). SongManager gains an optional 'string? databasePath = null' ctor arg (defaults to AppDatabase.DefaultPath, so existing 2-arg call sites keep compiling). SaveSongAsync upserts the row AFTER writing the authoritative song.json; LoadAllSongsAsync upserts the loaded songs and prunes vanished rows AFTER the existing folder-scan + registry load. A one-time defensive import populates the table from on-disk song.json files when the table is empty. ALL DB work is best-effort/try-catch-swallow so a DB failure never changes file behavior or the in-memory Songs list. BackupSongJson rotation and _song_registry.json are left completely untouched on disk. song.json files and audio stems remain authoritative on disk. SongLibraryService reads stay in-memory and need no change. Independent of FEAT-002 at the code level (different tables/methods), but ordered first because it is the structurally hardest and FEAT-002 reuses its EnsureInitialized/AppDatabase wiring.
steps: Read FIRST (absolute worktree paths): .agents/tasks/sql-phase06/context.json and this file; then WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/ServiceOrderManager.cs (the mirror precedent), WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/SongManager.cs (target), WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/SongPathResolver.cs, WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/AppDatabase.cs, WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/SongUsageService.cs. Do not re-derive what context.json already states.

In WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/SongManager.cs: add 'using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite;'. Add fields 'private readonly AppDatabase _database;' and 'private bool _initialized = false;'. Change the constructor to 'public SongManager(string songsBasePath, string setlistsBasePath, string? databasePath = null)' and set '_database = new AppDatabase(databasePath ?? AppDatabase.DefaultPath);' (keep the existing _jsonOptions exactly as-is — it is the serializer the mirror must reuse).

Add the Songs DDL as a const string: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Songs (FolderPath TEXT PRIMARY KEY, Title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', Artist TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', OriginalKey TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', Ccli TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', Themes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', Bpm REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, LastWriteUtc TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', DataJson TEXT NOT NULL);

Add private async EnsureInitializedAsync() mirroring ServiceOrderManager.EnsureInitializedAsync: guard on _initialized, call _database.EnsureDirectory(), open a connection, run the Songs DDL, then call the one-time import, then set _initialized = true.

Add a private key helper that returns SongPathResolver.Normalize(song.FolderPath) and a BindSong(SqliteCommand, Song, normalizedKey) that fills @FolderPath (normalized), @Title, @Artist, @OriginalKey, @Ccli, @Themes, @Bpm, @LastWriteUtc (File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc on <folder>/song.json when it exists else UtcNow, ISO-8601 'o'), and @DataJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(song, _jsonOptions). Add UpsertSongRowAsync(connection, transaction, song) using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(FolderPath) DO UPDATE SET of every non-key column (copy the ON CONFLICT shape from ServiceOrderManager.UpsertRowAsync).

Add UpsertSongRowSafeAsync(Song) and ReconcileSongsSafeAsync(IReadOnlyList<Song> loaded): both try/catch-and-swallow (comment: song.json is authoritative; a mirror failure must never break public behavior). ReconcileSongsSafeAsync opens a transaction, upserts each loaded song, then deletes rows whose FolderPath is NOT IN the normalized keys of the loaded set (parameterized NOT IN list, DELETE all when the set is empty) — copy ServiceOrderManager.ReconcileSafeAsync exactly, substituting Songs/FolderPath/Song.

In SaveSongAsync: after 'await File.WriteAllTextAsync(songJsonPath, json);' add 'await UpsertSongRowSafeAsync(song);'. Do NOT reorder or alter the BackupSongJson call or the song.json write — the mirror upsert runs strictly after the authoritative write.

In LoadAllSongsAsync: after the existing folder scan AND after 'await LoadSongsFromRegistryAsync();', add 'await ReconcileSongsSafeAsync(Songs);' so the mirror reflects exactly the songs that ended up in the in-memory list (dedup already applied). Do not change the scan, the dedup, or the registry logic.

Add the one-time defensive import ImportSongsIfNeededAsync(SqliteConnection): if Directory.Exists(_songsBasePath) is false return; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Songs, if > 0 return; open a transaction; for each subdir with a song.json, deserialize with _jsonOptions, set song.FolderPath = dir, INSERT OR IGNORE a mirror row via BindSong; also read _song_registry.json (if present) and import any referenced external folders' song.json the same way (skip missing dirs/files, skip paths already inserted); wrap per-file parsing in try/catch so one malformed file is skipped and the rest continue; wrap the whole method body in try/catch so it never throws (copy ServiceOrderManager.ImportFilesIfNeededAsync shape). Leave all JSON files on disk; do NOT touch backups or the registry file.

Confirm BackupSongJson (song.json.N rotation), RestoreBackupAsync, GetAvailableBackups, RegisterSongPathAsync, LoadSongsFromRegistryAsync, CreateSongFromFolder, and RemoveSong are left behaviorally identical (no mirror calls added to RemoveSong — the removed row is pruned on the next LoadAllSongsAsync reconcile, matching the Phase-5 out-of-band-delete absorption).
acceptance_criteria: SongManager compiles with the new optional databasePath arg; every existing 2-arg call site (MainWindow.xaml.cs:131 and all test fixtures) still compiles unchanged.

After SaveSongAsync, app.db Songs has exactly one row keyed by SongPathResolver.Normalize(FolderPath) whose DataJson round-trips to the saved Song (sections/tracks/midiCues/chordChart/metadata intact).
song.json is still written first and remains authoritative; song.json.N backups and _song_registry.json are byte-for-byte unaffected by the mirror.
A DB failure (e.g., unwritable db path) does not throw out of SaveSongAsync/LoadAllSongsAsync and does not alter the in-memory Songs list.
On a fresh app.db with on-disk song folders, the first LoadAllSongsAsync (or first init) imports one row per song; a second load does not duplicate rows.
Build is clean: 0 errors, exactly the 4 pre-existing warnings.
The targeted song test suite still passes at the baseline count (parity).
